title: Region-sticky session affinity + KV fanout shedding playbook
creator: Arielle Chen
description: Problem: In cross-region inference traffic, downstream stores (Redis/Kafka/Postgres) exhibit transient saturation that causes tail latency spikes and cascading failures. Existing connection pools and fallbacks are coarse-grained: when a region experiences degraded stores we either route all traffic away (costly) or return errors (bad UX). This ticket creates a playbook and a small control-plane + runtime changes to enable region-sticky session affinity, windowed fanout shedding for KV and stream requests, tenant-aware pool trimming, and SLO-driven graceful degradation policies.
motivation: Reduce customer-visible errors and tail latency during partial downstream saturation while preserving cost and keeping predictable SLOs. Allow regional failures to be mitigated without full failover, by selectively degrading non-critical or low-value operations and smoothing hot-key pressure.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can tag requests with region-sticky session id and honor stickiness with configurable TTL
Fanout to KV/store supports a windowed admission controller that drops or consolidates non-critical fanout requests when per-shard QPS or latency breach thresholds
Per-tenant connection pools support 'trim' API to reduce active connections proportionally to tenant priority
SLO-driven policies can be configured per-route: degrade to cached/approximate path, fall back to compact responses, or return synthetic placeholders
End-to-end e2e test demonstrating multi-region partial store failure and graceful degradation without full failover
implementation_notes: Add request affinity token in routing header (x-rw-affinity) and store mapping in routing table with TTL and refresh heuristics
Implement windowed fanout controller with 1s buckets; controller computes per-shard pressure metric combining p95 latency and queue length
Introduce pool.trim(percentage, reason) RPC to connection-pool manager, enforced asynchronously with soft-handoff to avoid storms
Expose SLO signals as feature flags per-customer to try conservative rollout
Provide fallback handlers: cached_prefix_hit -> condensed_response -> placeholder; decider chooses highest-quality allowed by configured degradation level
risks: Increased complexity in routing may interact with existing canary rollouts and break A/B tests unless we add test-only overrides
Affinity tokens create stickiness that could concentrate load on under-provisioned shards (mitigated by short TTL + proactive rebalance),
Trimming connections too aggressively may increase queueing and head-of-line latency if misconfigured
Fallback/approximate responses risk silent quality regressions — must tie to eval prompt sets and monitor model-output diffs
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind runtime.feature.region_affinity (off by default)
Start with internal test org + 2 low-risk customers for 72h burn-in
Enable fanout shedding in permissive mode (observability-only) to tune thresholds for 7 days
Progress to progressive ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 4 cycles if no SLO regressions
Expose manual emergency kill-switch and automatic rollback if SLO < configured baseline for 15m
test_plan: Unit tests for pool.trim and controller heuristics
Integration: chaos test simulating Redis hot-shard (90th percentile latency spike) and verify windowed shedding reduces client p99 failures
E2E: deploy to staging multiregion with injected cross-region latency and verify degraded responses are tagged and audited
Load test with synthetic tenants to validate proportional trimming logic and fairness
